sections.title: Level 2 Concept Overview
sections.content: Level 2 Pattern Completion involves more complex logic than Level 1. Questions usually include a 3x3 matrix, combination of figures, rotation of elements, and shading changes. Students must carefully analyze both row-wise and column-wise patterns before deciding the missing figure.

sections.title: 3x3 Matrix (Nine-Box Grid)
sections.content:
In a 3x3 grid, eight boxes are given and the ninth (usually bottom-right) is missing.
Solution Steps:
1. Observe the pattern across the first row.
2. Apply the same rule to the second and third rows.
3. Now check the pattern column-wise.
4. The missing box must satisfy both row and column logic.

sections.title: Combination / Addition Rule
sections.content:
Sometimes Figure 1 and Figure 2 combine to form Figure 3. In some cases, common lines or overlapping parts are removed.
Solution Steps:
1. Mentally superimpose Figure 1 and Figure 2.
2. Identify overlapping or common parts.
3. Remove common parts if required.
4. Apply the same logic in the next row or column.

sections.title: Rotation Pattern
sections.content:
Arrows or internal lines may rotate 90° or 45° clockwise or anticlockwise across rows or columns.
Solution Steps:
1. Compare the direction change between first two figures.
2. Identify the angle and direction of rotation.
3. Check if the same rotation continues.
4. Apply it to find the missing figure.

sections.title: Shading / Coloring Pattern
sections.content:
Black and white shaded regions may alternate or shift positions.
Solution Steps:
1. Observe shading movement across the row.
2. Check if shading alternates (black-white-black).
3. Verify if the same pattern applies column-wise.
4. Choose the figure that fits both directions.

sections.title: Row-wise and Column-wise Verification
sections.content: At Level 2, the pattern may differ in rows and columns. For example, rows may follow addition logic while columns follow rotation logic. Always confirm the missing figure satisfies both rules.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Ignoring column-wise logic.
2. Misjudging the rotation angle.
3. Forgetting to remove common elements in combination questions.
4. Overlooking small shading shifts.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 requires 3–4 logical steps. Carefully analyze rows, then columns, check rotation and combination rules, and ensure the final figure satisfies all observed patterns.

tricks.title: Row First, Column Next
tricks.explanation: Always decode the row pattern before checking the column pattern.
tricks.example: If shapes increase across the row, confirm whether columns rotate or shift.

tricks.title: Superimpose Mentally
tricks.explanation: Visualize overlapping figures to detect addition or deletion rules.
tricks.example: Two lines overlapping may disappear in the third figure.

tricks.title: Track Rotation Direction
tricks.explanation: Identify whether rotation is clockwise or anticlockwise.
tricks.example: Up → Right → Down suggests 90° clockwise rotation.

tricks.title: Observe Shading Flow
tricks.explanation: Shaded parts may move step by step in one direction.
tricks.example: Top shaded → Right shaded → Bottom shaded.

tricks.title: Look for Fixed Elements
tricks.explanation: Some parts remain constant while others change.
tricks.example: Outer square remains same; inner arrow rotates.

tricks.title: Diagonal Check
tricks.explanation: Sometimes a pattern follows diagonal movement.
tricks.example: Top-left and center may share similar rotation.

tricks.title: Eliminate Incomplete Matches
tricks.explanation: Remove options that match only one rule but fail the other.
tricks.example: Correct rotation but wrong shading should be eliminated.
